title: The Influence of Including Goalkeepers On The Intensity Demands Of Walking Football Practice
content: This study examined the effects of playing walking football with and without a goalkeeper (GK) on physiological, physical, technical, and perceptual variables in older men. Twenty participants (67 ± 4.7 years) engaged in two 5 vs. 5 walking football sessions: one WITH-GK and one WITH-OUT-GK, using a randomized crossover design. Heart rate (HR), distance covered, technical ac-tions, perceived exercise intensity, and enjoyment were measured. Results showed significantly higher average HR (131 bpm vs. 123 bpm, p < .001), %HRmax (79% vs. 74%, p < .001), and time in higher HR zones (>80%HRmax, p < .05) in the WITH-GK condition. Participants also covered more total distance in the WITH-GK condition (1123 m vs. 1083 m, p < .001), particularly at speeds above 4 km/h (834 m vs. 781 m, p < .001). Conversely, more passes were made in the WITHOUT-GK condition (20 vs. 16 passes, p < .001), while the WITH-GK condition showed more shots (2 vs. 1, p < .001). Perceived exercise intensity was slightly higher in the WITH-OUT-GK condition (5 vs. 4, p = .01), though enjoyment levels were similar, with a slight preference for WITHOUT-GK. Overall, playing WITHOUT-GK provides a safer, lower-intensity alternative to WITH-GK, reducing physical strain while maintaining enjoyment. This makes WITHOUT-GK particularly suitable for older adults or individuals with health conditions, promoting partici-pation and rehabilitation with minimized risks.
